method: Each claim checked against the retrieved text of the ACSQHC Cataract Clinical Care Standard (published 2021), including all eight quality statements, the for-clinicians/for-services/for-consumers sections and the indicator list. Every source_text fragment was machine-checked verbatim with scripts/verify.py. Boxes 1, 2 and 3 (assessment tools for vision-related activity limitation, referral components, prioritisation tools) are in the full PDF, referenced repeatedly and not retrieved. The intracameral cefazolin DOSE is in Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic, which is licensed content cited by reference and not reproduced; only 'a single dose at the end of surgery' is stated by this source. The source spells anisometropia as 'anisemotropia'; source_text is preserved verbatim and the guideline renders the evident word. Source URL recorded at retrieval.

claims.claim: Cataract is a condition that can cause problems with vision when the lens of the eye becomes cloudy, is more common in older people, and is a considerable problem for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander populations
claims.source_text: Cataract is a condition that can cause problems with vision when the lens of the eye becomes cloudy. It is more common in older people, and is a considerable problem for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander populations.

claims.claim: Cataract is the most common elective surgery diagnosis in Australia
claims.source_text: Cataract is the most common elective surgery diagnosis in Australia.

claims.claim: The Cataract Clinical Care Standard was published in 2021
claims.source_text: The Cataract Clinical Care Standard was published in 2021 and includes:

claims.claim: Quality statement 1 states that a patient with visual problems and suspected cataract has an initial assessment in primary care of their visual impairment, vision-related activity limitations, comorbidities and willingness to have surgery, and that when referral is appropriate based on these criteria the patient is referred for consideration for cataract surgery with this information included in the referral form
claims.source_text: A patient with visual problems and suspected cataract has an initial assessment in primary care of their visual impairment, vision-related activity limitations, comorbidities and willingness to have surgery. When referral is appropriate based on these criteria, the patient is referred for consideration for cataract surgery, and this information is included in the referral form.

claims.claim: A patient with visual problems due to suspected cataract requires an ocular examination preferably performed using a slit lamp biomicroscope or direct ophthalmoscope and an assessment of how their visual problems are affecting their life, and optometry referral may be a suitable initial option for assessment of cataract
claims.source_text: A patient with visual problems due to suspected cataract requires an ocular examination, preferably performed using a slit lamp biomicroscope or direct ophthalmoscope, and an assessment of how their visual problems are affecting their life. Optometry referral may be a suitable initial option for assessment of cataract.

claims.claim: Clinicians should advise the patient that the presence of cataract alone is not an indication for surgery, and patients with lens opacities that do not cause visual symptoms or limit daily activities can continue to be managed and monitored in the primary care setting
claims.source_text: Discuss the possible options to manage the patient's symptoms and advise them that the presence of cataract alone is not an indication for surgery. Patients with lens opacities that do not cause visual symptoms or limit daily activities can continue to be managed and monitored in the primary care setting.

claims.claim: Referral for possible cataract surgery should be considered when patients have visual impairment that interferes with their ability to carry out their usual daily tasks, considering the possible impact on their ability to live independently
claims.source_text: Consider referral for possible cataract surgery when patients have visual impairment that interferes with their ability to carry out their usual daily tasks, considering the possible impact on their ability to live independently.

claims.claim: Visual impairment can include reduced visual acuity or disabling glare or contrast sensitivity, and vision-related activity limitations may include a loss of ability to work, drive, carry out daily tasks, or care for themselves or others, for example an increased risk of falls in older people with risk factors
claims.source_text: Visual impairment can include reduced visual acuity, or disabling glare or contrast sensitivity. Vision-related activity limitations may include a loss of ability to work, drive, carry out daily tasks, or care for themselves or others - for example, an increased risk of falls in older people with risk factors.

claims.claim: If the patient does not want to consider cataract surgery and there are no other indications for ophthalmology assessment, referral to an ophthalmology service may not be appropriate, and support should be provided to reduce the impact of their visual problems including refractive correction, tinted lenses to reduce glare, or use of suitable equipment to optimise vision
claims.source_text: If the patient does not to want to consider cataract surgery and there are no other indications for ophthalmology assessment, referral to an ophthalmology service may not be appropriate. Provide support for patients to reduce the impact of their visual problems, including refractive correction, tinted lenses to reduce glare, or use of suitable equipment to optimise vision and improve the patient's capacity for activities of daily living.

claims.claim: A standardised referral template can be effective for improving the appropriateness of referral as well as improving the quality of information needed to triage patients for ophthalmology appointments
claims.source_text: A standardised referral template can be effective for improving the appropriateness of referral, as well as improving the quality of information needed to triage patients for ophthalmology appointments.

claims.claim: Quality statement 2 states that a patient with suspected or confirmed cataract receives information to support shared decision making, that information is provided in a way that meets the patient's needs and is easy to use and understand, and that the patient is given the opportunity to discuss the likely benefits and potential harms of the available options as well as their needs and preferences
claims.source_text: A patient with suspected or confirmed cataract receives information to support shared decision making. Information is provided in a way that meets the patient's needs, and is easy to use and understand. The patient is given the opportunity to discuss the likely benefits and potential harms of the available options, as well as their needs and preferences.

claims.claim: Patients should be provided with clinically accurate evidence-based information about their options both verbally and in a written format that is easy to use, for example in large font or electronically, and suitable options may include surgical or non-surgical options such as visual aids or watchful waiting
claims.source_text: Provide patients who have cataract with clinically accurate, evidence-based information about their options, both verbally and in a written format that is easy to use - for example, in large font or electronically. Suitable options may include surgical or non-surgical options, such as visual aids or watchful waiting.

claims.claim: The level of comorbidities in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, their age at diagnosis and disparities in their health outcomes means that health care for this population needs to be refocused to meet the unique needs of each patient
claims.source_text: The level of comorbidities in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, their age at diagnosis and disparities in their health outcomes means that health care for this population needs to be refocused to meet the unique needs of each patient.

claims.claim: Quality statement 3 states that a patient who has been referred for consideration for cataract surgery is prioritised for ophthalmology assessment according to clinical need based on a locally approved protocol and following receipt of a detailed referral
claims.source_text: A patient who has been referred for consideration for cataract surgery is prioritised for ophthalmology assessment according to clinical need, based on a locally approved protocol and following receipt of a detailed referral.

claims.claim: Clinicians should use an agreed local protocol to allocate appointments for referred patients, prioritising them according to clinical need including social and cultural circumstances and barriers to accessing care
claims.source_text: Use an agreed local protocol to allocate appointments for referred patients, prioritising them according to clinical need, including social and cultural circumstances and barriers to accessing care.

claims.claim: Referrals should be reviewed by a credentialed ophthalmic clinician who can use the information in the referral to make an initial assessment about the appropriateness of referral, severity of symptoms and relative priority for ophthalmological assessment
claims.source_text: Referrals should be reviewed by a credentialed ophthalmic clinician who can use the information in the referral to make an initial assessment about the appropriateness of referral, severity of symptoms and relative priority for ophthalmological assessment.

claims.claim: Processes should be in place to monitor patients waiting for first ophthalmology appointments in case their clinical needs and priority change
claims.source_text: Processes should be in place to monitor patients waiting for first ophthalmology appointments in case their clinical needs and priority change.

claims.claim: Indicator 3a is evidence of a locally approved protocol to allocate appointments for patients considering cataract surgery, and indicator 3b is the proportion of referrals received that included the required patient information
claims.source_text: | Indicator 3a | Evidence of a locally approved protocol to allocate appointments for patients considering cataract surgery | … | Indicator 3b | Proportion of referrals for consideration for cataract surgery received that included the required patient information |

claims.claim: Indicator 3c is the proportion of patients referred for consideration for cataract surgery that did not meet the criteria for referral, and indicator 3d is the proportion of patients referred for cataract surgery who had cataract surgery
claims.source_text: | Indicator 3c | Proportion of patients referred for consideration for cataract surgery that did not meet the criteria for referral | … | Indicator 3d | Proportion of patients referred for cataract surgery who had cataract surgery |

claims.claim: Quality statement 4 states that a patient is offered cataract surgery when they have a lens opacity that limits their vision-related activities and causes clinically significant visual impairment involving reduced best corrected visual acuity, disabling glare or contrast sensitivity
claims.source_text: A patient is offered cataract surgery when they have a lens opacity that limits their vision-related activities and causes clinically significant visual impairment involving reduced best corrected visual acuity, disabling glare or contrast sensitivity.

claims.claim: The statement applies to people having cataract surgery primarily to improve vision and does not apply to other indications including angle closure and phacolytic glaucoma or to allow monitoring of retinal conditions
claims.source_text: This statement applies to people having cataract surgery primarily to improve vision. … It does not apply to other indications for cataract surgery including angle closure and phacolytic glaucoma, or to allow monitoring of retinal conditions.

claims.claim: Visual acuity of 6/12 or worse may provide a useful objective measure of visual impairment but may significantly underestimate function, for example in conditions of high or low light, glare or contrast sensitivity may be disabling without an impact on visual acuity, and some patients will have higher visual acuity needs such as for occupational activities
claims.source_text: Visual acuity of 6/12 or worse may provide a useful objective measure of visual impairment, but may significantly underestimate function - for example, in conditions of high or low light. Glare or contrast sensitivity may be disabling without an impact on visual acuity. Some patients will have higher visual acuity needs, such as for occupational activities.

claims.claim: Most patients have an improvement in visual function after surgery, and patients most likely to report a poor outcome after surgery include those with good self-assessed preoperative visual function
claims.source_text: Most patients have an improvement in visual function after surgery. Patients most likely to report a poor outcome after surgery include those with good self-assessed preoperative visual function.

claims.claim: Clinicians should consider conditions that increase the risk of complications or a poor outcome from cataract surgery such as diabetes, diabetic retinopathy or uveitis, or that limit the extent of visual gain such as age-related macular degeneration
claims.source_text: Consider conditions that increase the risk of complications or a poor outcome from cataract surgery (such as diabetes, diabetic retinopathy or uveitis) or limit the extent of visual gain (such as age-related macular degeneration).

claims.claim: Quality statement 5 states that a patient is prioritised for cataract surgery according to clinical need and that prioritisation protocols take into account the severity of the patient's visual impairment and vision-related activity limitations, the potential harms of delayed surgery, any relevant comorbidity and the expected benefits of surgery
claims.source_text: A patient is prioritised for cataract surgery according to clinical need. Prioritisation protocols take into account the severity of the patient's visual impairment and vision-related activity limitations, the potential harms of delayed surgery, any relevant comorbidity and the expected benefits of surgery.

claims.claim: Prioritisation protocols should enable those patients at greatest risk of harm from delayed surgery and those most likely to benefit to be treated first, potential harms of delayed surgery include risks of falls or traffic accidents or increased complexity of later surgery for example in patients with densely brunescent or white cataract, and social factors including remoteness, language and culture should also be considered
claims.source_text: Prioritisation protocols should enable those patients at greatest risk of harm from delayed surgery and those who are most likely to benefit from surgery to be treated first. Potential harms associated with delayed surgery include risks of falls or traffic accidents, or increased complexity of later surgery - for example, in patients with densely brunescent or white cataract. Social factors that may affect the ability of patients to access care, should also be considered, including remoteness, language and culture.

claims.claim: Comorbid conditions that may increase the urgency of cataract surgery include acute angle glaucoma and posterior segment disease where fundal access is required for monitoring or treatment
claims.source_text: Comorbid conditions that may increase the urgency of cataract surgery should be considered in the prioritisation process. These include acute angle glaucoma and posterior segment disease, where fundal access is required for monitoring or treatment.

claims.claim: Indicator 5a is evidence of a locally approved protocol to prioritise patients for cataract surgery according to clinical need
claims.source_text: | Indicator 5a | Evidence of a locally approved protocol to prioritise patients for cataract surgery according to clinical need |

claims.claim: Quality statement 6 states that options for a patient with bilateral cataract are discussed when the decision about first-eye surgery is being made, that second-eye surgery is offered using similar criteria as for the first eye but with the potential benefits and harms of a delay also considered, leading to a shared decision about second-eye surgery and its timing
claims.source_text: Options for a patient with bilateral cataract are discussed when the decision about first-eye surgery is being made. Second-eye surgery is offered using similar criteria as for the first eye, but the potential benefits and harms of a delay in second-eye surgery are also considered, leading to a shared decision about second-eye surgery and its timing.

claims.claim: Clinicians should consider existing or anticipated anisometropia after first-eye surgery and its impact on vision and visual function including stereopsis, stereoacuity and falls risk
claims.source_text: In addition, consider existing or anticipated anisemotropia (a significant difference in refractive error between the two eyes) after first-eye surgery, and its impact on vision and visual function, including stereopsis (depth perception), stereoacuity and falls risk.

claims.claim: Having second-eye surgery later allows complete postoperative recovery and if needed treatment of postoperative complications from first-eye surgery, and the opportunity to assess and plan surgery based on the results of first-eye surgery
claims.source_text: Having second-eye surgery later allows complete postoperative recovery (and, if needed, treatment of postoperative complications) from first-eye surgery, and the opportunity to assess and plan surgery based on the results of first-eye surgery.

claims.claim: There is limited evidence to support second-eye surgery on the same or next day, and it may be considered for patients at low risk of complications during and after surgery or at risk from delayed second eye surgery, to avoid a second general anaesthetic when general anaesthetic is required, and for whom distance and travel are considerable barriers such as in remote and very remote areas
claims.source_text: There is limited evidence to support second-eye surgery on the same or next day.It may be considered for patients … - at low risk of complications during and after surgery, or at risk from delayed second eye surgery … - to avoid a second general anaesthetic, when general anaesthetic is required … - for whom distance and travel are considerable barriers, such as in remote and very remote areas.

claims.claim: Patients should be informed of the consequences of complications including the risk of potentially blinding complications in both eyes such as endophthalmitis or toxic anterior segment syndrome
claims.source_text: Ensure that patients are informed of the consequences of complications, including the risk of potentially blinding complications in both eyes, such as endophthalmitis or toxic anterior segment syndrome.

claims.claim: Quality statement 7 states that a patient receives an intracameral antibiotic injection at the time of cataract surgery in preference to postoperative topical antibiotics and according to evidence-based guidelines, and that after surgery a patient receives anti-inflammatory eye drops when indicated
claims.source_text: A patient receives an intracameral antibiotic injection at the time of cataract surgery, in preference to postoperative topical antibiotics and according to evidence-based guidelines. After surgery, a patient receives anti-inflammatory eye drops when indicated.

claims.claim: Evidence-based guidelines recommend intracameral antibiotics for endophthalmitis prophylaxis in preference to topical pre- or postoperative antibiotic eye drops, Therapeutic Guidelines Antibiotic recommends cefazolin intracamerally as a single dose at the end of surgery and avoiding quinolones or vancomycin which lack evidence, and prophylactic use of topical antibiotic solutions or eye drops is not recommended with little evidence to support their use
claims.source_text: Evidence-based guidelines recommend use of intracameral antibiotics for endophthalmitis prophylaxis in preference to topical pre- or postoperative antibiotic eye drops. Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic recommend cefazolin intracamerally as a single dose at the end of surgery, and avoiding use of quinolones or vancomycin, which lack evidence; consider the risk of antibiotic resistance. Prophylactic use of topical antibiotic solutions or eye drops is not recommended, and there is little evidence to support their use.

claims.claim: If no commercially prepared intracameral formulation is available antibiotic eye drops may be considered to avoid the risk of dilution errors and contamination, advice should be sought for patients with hypersensitivity to penicillin or cephalosporins, and if postoperative antibiotic eye drops are used chloramphenicol 0.5 per cent eye drops are recommended with the duration stipulated to a maximum of seven days to avoid overuse
claims.source_text: If no commercially prepared intracameral formulation is available, antibiotic eye drops may be considered to avoid the risk of dilution errors and contamination. Seek advice in the case of patients with hypersensitivity to penicillin or cephalosporins.If postoperative antibiotic eye drops are used, chloramphenicol 0.5% eye drops are recommended. Stipulate the duration (maximum seven days) to avoid overuse.

claims.claim: Postoperative anti-inflammatory eye drops being corticosteroid eye drops with or without non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs should be considered for patients at high risk of developing cystoid macular oedema after cataract surgery such as patients with diabetic retinopathy or other high-risk ocular comorbidities
claims.source_text: Consider postoperative anti-inflammatory eye drops (corticosteroid eye drops, with or without non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) for patients at high risk of developing cystoid macular oedema after cataract surgery, such as patients with diabetic retinopathy or other high-risk ocular comorbidities.

claims.claim: Potential adverse effects include allergic reactions to antibiotics, increased intraocular pressure with corticosteroids and rarely epithelial damage with non-steroidal anti-inflammatories
claims.source_text: Potential adverse effects include allergic reactions to antibiotics, increased intraocular pressure with corticosteroids and, rarely, epithelial damage with non-steroidal anti-inflammatories.

claims.claim: Intracameral use of cefazolin is off-label and its addition to the formulary will need to be approved by the local Drugs and Therapeutics Committee under routine use of an off-label medicine
claims.source_text: Intracameral use of cefazolin is off-label, and its addition to the formulary will need to be approved by the local Drugs and Therapeutics Committee under routine use of an off-label medicine.

claims.claim: Indicator 7a is the proportion of patients who received intracameral administration of antibiotics at the end of surgery
claims.source_text: | Indicator 7a | Proportion of patients who received intracameral administration of antibiotics at the end of surgery |

claims.claim: Quality statement 8 states that a patient receives postoperative care that ensures the early detection and treatment of complications of cataract surgery and the patient's visual rehabilitation, that postoperative care is provided by the operating ophthalmologist or a designated team member, and that the patient is informed of the arrangements for postoperative care
claims.source_text: A patient receives postoperative care that ensures the early detection and treatment of complications of cataract surgery, and the patient's visual rehabilitation. Postoperative care is provided by the operating ophthalmologist or a designated team member. The patient is informed of the arrangements for postoperative care.

claims.claim: Clinicians should determine the exact frequency of postoperative review taking into account the surgical technique, any operative or postoperative complications and the person's ability to access care, and early review within 24 hours may be warranted for patients at high risk of complications
claims.source_text: Determine the exact frequency of postoperative review, taking into account the surgical technique, any operative or postoperative complications, and the person's ability to access care. Early review (within 24 hours) may be warranted for patients at high risk of complica
